blocks.text: After organizing a three-day fast among the Jews of Susa and fasting with her young women, Esther executes the risky uninvited approach to the king described in this chapter. In Esther 5:1-2, she dresses in her royal apparel and stands in the inner court positioned before the king's throne. The king's immediate response—extending the golden scepter to her—signals favor and grants her access to his presence.
